not_found: Lifetime of 5p3(4S°)7p 5P1: Zerne et al. 1994 give 128(11) ns for '7p 5P1', but NIST lists two levels, a 5P1 at 63556.707 and b 5P1 at 63669.944 cm-1 (the site draws the second); the abstract does not say which one was measured, so the value is not attached to a level.

Lifetimes of the 5p3 6s 5S°2 (44253.000) and 3S°1 (46652.738) resonance levels: no measurement could be opened. Ubelis & Berzinsh, Phys. Scr. 43, 162 (1991) (transition probabilities of 20 Te I lines by the Ladenburg method, normalised to known 6s lifetimes) - only the abstract (https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/5622530) was readable, it prints no numbers.
Hyperfine constants of 123Te and 125Te (I = 1/2) in any Te I level: none found in an openable source (Ross & Murakawa, Phys. Rev. 85, 559 (1952) is paywalled).

Isotope shifts of the 214.28 nm line (COMPLIS: Sifi et al., Hyperfine Interact. 171, 173 (2006), 120-136Te): paper and the ISOLDE proposal INTC-P-561 could not be opened (publisher paywall / bot protection).

Lifetimes of the metastable 5p4 3P1, 3P0, 1D2, 1S0 levels and A values of the forbidden lines (e.g. 3P2-1D2 at 947 nm, drawn by the site): no measurement located; Biémont et al. 1995 calculations are cited by Mulholland et al. (arXiv:2410.05958) but no table of Te I forbidden A values was found there.
Precise transition frequencies, laser-cooling or clock lines: none located for neutral Te.
notes: Thin file: neutral Te has little modern precision spectroscopy in open sources. The three lifetimes come from an abstract (OSTI/ETDEWEB record of Z. Phys. D 32, 31), read through an automated page reader and not checked against the printed paper. NIST carries A values for six 5p4 - 5p3 6s lines (Ubelis & Berzinsh); nothing better was found. Abundances: NIST isotopic compositions (120Te 0.09(1) %, 130Te 34.08(62) %).
